q: What's the difference between RANK() and DENSE_RANK()?
opts: RANK leaves gaps after ties (1,2,2,4), DENSE_RANK doesn't (1,2,2,3).
RANK is for windows, DENSE_RANK is for aggregations.
RANK is older SQL standard; DENSE_RANK is newer.
explain: RANK = gaps after ties; DENSE_RANK = no gaps.

q: Why is NOT IN (subquery) dangerous when the subquery can return NULL?
opts: NULL in subquery makes the whole NOT IN return zero rows.
NULL is treated as a regular value.
NOT IN ignores NULLs by default.
explain: Three-valued logic: 'x NOT IN (1, NULL)' is NULL, not true. Use NOT EXISTS.

q: What's the canonical dedupe-by-latest pattern in SQL?
opts: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
explain: ROW_NUMBER + filter rn=1 preserves all columns of the chosen row.

q: Which tables ALWAYS require WHERE __is_deleted = false?
opts: The kafka_cdc tables: accounts, jobs, sites, etc.
Only dim_accounts in the dbt project.
explain: Production bug if you skip __is_deleted on CDC tables. Staging doesn't always propagate it.

q: An incremental dbt model on a 100M-row table is duplicating rows after a backfill. Most likely cause?
opts: Missing unique_key in the config — append vs merge.
The table has too many partitions.
explain: Without unique_key + merge strategy, incremental just appends — backfill = duplicates.

q: What is grain in dimensional modeling?
opts: What one row in the fact table represents.
The compression ratio of the table.
explain: Grain = the meaning of a single row. Every fact has one declared grain.

q: When would you use SCD Type 2 over Type 1?
opts: When historical accuracy of the attribute matters at the time of the fact.
When you want to save storage.
explain: Type 2 keeps versioned rows; Type 1 overwrites — losing history.

q: In Spark, you call df.filter(...).groupBy(...). No computation happens. Why?
opts: Transformations are lazy — only actions trigger execution.
explain: Spark builds a logical plan; only actions like .show(), .collect(), .write() execute.

q: Why is a broadcast hash join faster than a sort-merge join?
opts: No shuffle — small side broadcast to all executors.
It runs only on the driver.
explain: Broadcast skips the network shuffle; each executor joins locally with the small table.

q: What does Delta Lake's transaction log enable that raw Parquet on S3 doesn't?
opts: ACID transactions, time travel, schema evolution.
explain: _delta_log/ is the ordered commit history. Parquet alone has no transaction semantics.

q: Slim CI in dbt is achieved with:
explain: state:modified+ builds changed models + downstream only — typical 10× CI speed up.

q: You see one Spark task taking 50× longer than others in the same stage. Diagnosis?
opts: Data skew — one key has disproportionate rows.
explain: Skew shows as one straggler task. Fix: AQE skew handling, salting, or broadcast.

q: Which dbt test would catch 'every order_id in fct_order_items exists in fct_orders'?
explain: relationships = referential integrity / FK check across models.

q: What makes a pipeline idempotent?
opts: Same input always produces the same output, regardless of how many times run.
It can run only once per day.
It runs in under a second.
explain: Idempotency = safe retries and backfills. Achieved via MERGE or delete-then-insert per partition.

q: What does VACUUM on a Delta table do?
opts: Removes data files older than retention period that are no longer referenced.
explain: VACUUM frees storage from old versions; OPTIMIZE compacts small files. Different ops.

q: Where does the AE typically fix a wrong metric?
opts: At the canonical dbt model, with a test added to prevent regression.
In the Tableau workbook with a custom calc.
In the BI semantic layer only.
Manually each time it comes up.
explain: Fix upstream; tests prevent regression; every downstream consumer benefits.

q: What's the safe alternative to NOT IN with nullable subqueries?
explain: NOT EXISTS is NULL-safe; correlated existence check returns true/false only.

q: Conventional Commits format used in PRs?
explain: Type prefix + ticket reference, imperative description. A common convention.

q: What's the silver layer in medallion architecture?
opts: Cleaned, conformed, joined data — roughly staging+intermediate.
explain: Bronze=raw, Silver=cleaned/conformed, Gold=business-ready aggregates.

q: When stakeholder says 'real-time' — what's the AE's first move?
opts: Clarify actual latency SLO; usually 5-minute micro-batch is sufficient.
explain: 'Real-time' often = 'sub-hour'. Match latency to actual need; streaming costs 10×.
